correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 the proof supplies a unique coordinate for every unordered pair, the exact two letter transitions including both parity-dependent diameter boundaries, and a finite-tail argument ensuring unique moment solutions. It verifies the first- and second-moment absorbing Bellman equations with explicit all-n polynomials and derives the aggregate second moment by power-sum identities. Both dependency-free verifiers check 85,320 pair states for n=2..80, and separate exact Fraction linear solves check 220 states per moment for n=2..11. Finite evidence is distinguished from the explicit all-integer argument.

originality.rationale: The closest exact primary source, Gusev (2014), establishes arbitrary-bias first moments and the maximum among pairs, not second moments. The new all-length sixth-degree variance law for a uniformly sampled pair is not implied by a formula specifying only first moments. Its proof solves a distinct moment Bellman equation and sums a nontrivial family of statewise potentials. Recent Černý works address deterministic/adversarial synchronization, not this law. Actual indexed queries revealed no covering result; unindexed prior work remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible publication might already compute the uniform-pair second moment or variance.

The full texts of the two SIAM synchronizing probability function papers were not inspected; their abstracts suggest a different process.
Independent mathematical review and exhaustive priority confirmation have not been performed.

value.rationale: The variance of synchronization delay is a natural reliability invariant not determined by the already-known mean. The result provides an exact all-size polynomial in a classical extremal family, and proves that its normalized standard deviation tends to a nonzero constant sqrt(7/5). It reflects fluctuations at the same cubic scale as the expectation and is neither a short finite census nor a textbook renaming.
